title: Check your understanding: Dataset Types & Temporal Dynamics

items.prompt: What are the two fundamental orthogonal axes used to categorize datasets in modern data engineering?
choices: Hardware architecture and GPU memory bandwidth
Structural organization (schema rigidity) and temporal dynamics (evolution over time)
Compression codec and encryption key length
items.explain: Datasets are categorized structurally (structured, semi-structured, unstructured) and temporally (static snapshots versus dynamic streams).

items.prompt: Which property is a mathematical requirement for structured tabular relations adhering to first normal form (1NF)?
choices: Attributes must contain variable-length nested dictionaries without keys
All attribute values in each cell must be atomic and indivisible, with homogeneous column types
Records must arrive out of order across streaming sockets
Every table must be stored exclusively in plain text CSV files
items.explain: First normal form requires that each attribute value is atomic, with uniform typing and schema conformity across all tuples.

items.prompt: In dynamic event streaming systems, what is the primary role of an event-time watermark?
choices: To encrypt sensitive customer identifiers before writing to disk
To provide a temporal threshold indicating that no earlier events are expected, allowing window aggregations to close
To compress audio waveforms into dense vector embeddings
To assign sequential primary keys to relational SQL tables
items.explain: Watermarks track event-time progression and define a heuristic boundary for handling late-arriving events so windowed aggregations can be finalized.

items.prompt: Unstructured data like audio and medical imaging can be queried directly using standard relational SQL joins without prior feature extraction or neural embedding models.
items.explain: Unstructured data lacks a uniform relational schema and requires deep feature extractors or embedding models to map raw signals into structured representation spaces.

items.prompt: Why do web applications often choose semi-structured formats like JSON over rigid relational tables for transaction payloads?
items.rubric: Allows flexible, self-describing schemas with nested objects and optional fields without requiring database schema migrations.
items.sample_answer: Semi-structured formats are self-describing and support hierarchical nesting and optional fields, allowing schemas to evolve without costly database migrations.
